rationale:
I accept the critique's main point: the baseline is reproducible, and the untested alternatives are risky on a final, unseen track. I also reject the draft's premise that it was delivering the iteration-5 design with wheel_track changed to 0.10. The outcome table shows that iteration 5 (score 137.7649) used body 0.18 x 0.12 m, mass 0.8 kg, sensors at y = 0.06 with x = -0.06 to +0.06, wheel_track 0.12, kp 3.0, ki 0.3, kd 0.4, base_speed 1.8 and last_direction line loss. The draft's authorized-input values (body 0.14 x 0.10, mass 0.5, sensors at y = 0.07, ki 0, base_speed 1.3) do not match any raced configuration on the scoreboard, so I treat them as an error and do not use them. Iterations 7 to 9 reproduced iteration 5's score exactly, which is the evidence that this exact design is reproducible.

What I kept: the decision to submit the verified 137.76 configuration rather than an untested change. The final race is scored on an unseen track, and no tested change beat 137.76. The critique's ki-offset idea is reasonable but was tested only weakly. ki 0.1 dropped the score to 105.5, and ki 0.6 dropped it to 122.2, so ki 0.3 is the best tested value and moving it is a gamble.

What I changed: only the wheel_track value. The raced design used 0.12, not 0.10 as the draft claimed, so I keep 0.12 so the result matches the record. Iterations 7 to 9 show that the metrics do not depend on the tested base_speed or wheel_track values, so this choice is about matching the tested configuration.

Expected result: about 137.8 on the development tracks (oval about 284 mean with two finishes, s-bend about 78, slalom about 52). The unseen track may differ, so this figure applies only to the development tracks. The design has no measured margin from the off-track limit, and I have no evidence about how it behaves on a new bend type.
